Section 4 cites [S12] for 'market capitalisation of IDR28,773.2bn at the last close' and for the house bank method set (50/30/20). The price and mcap are S0 data and the method weights are the VAL_BANKS card, not the annual report.

The coverage hole is carried twice: the base terminal credit cost 3.1% is set above the FY2023-25 loan-only average (~2.8%) 'because allowance coverage is only 27%', and the bear adds a permanent +1.3pp for the same rebuild. Using the 2.8% average would lift the justified P/BV leg and the target by roughly 20-30% (still SELL), so it is not rating-changing, but it is the same conservatism in base and bear.

The model's FY2025A history still reads the pack (NII 281.25, NOII 19.82, PPOP 186.34) against the audited NII 289.38 and NOII 42.68 (PPOP 217.33), a PPOP gap of 14%. Section 3 discloses the presentation gap in full and the forecast NII is built on the 8M run-rate (Rp250.4bn = 166.86 x 12/8) so there is no valuation error, but the audit trail is the model's, not the filing's.

flags.message: a.cti moves -5.6pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The ratio moves -5.6pp from FY2026E to FY2035E through the denominator, not through a cost cut. Opex follows one stated rupiah path: the audited FY2025A Rp114.726bn (F9) held flat in FY2026E, then +5% a year - Rp120.462bn in FY2027E, Rp139.450bn in FY2030E and Rp177.975bn in FY2035E [S12]. Total operating income grows from Rp271.2bn in FY2026E, which is the eight-month NII run-rate of Rp166.86bn annualised (F25) [S6] plus non-interest income, to Rp485.3bn by FY2035E as the funded balance sheet and the margin recover to the FY2025A ratio - 5.9% a year against 5.0% cost growth. The 5% cost growth is below the 6.2% actual FY2025 opex growth (F9 vs F10) [S12]; no cost programme is assumed and the FY2027E ratio rises to 43.0% because costs outgrow income that year.

flags.message: a.payout moves +30.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The step is created by the law, not by a dividend forecast: unappropriated retained earnings are a deficit of Rp253.748bn at end-2025 (F21, [S12]), so no distribution is legally available until cumulative profit clears it. Our FY2026E-FY2030E profits total about Rp240.8bn and leave about Rp12.9bn outstanding, so it is cleared during FY2031E and the first payout is on FY2031 profit. The 30% from FY2031 is consistent with terminal growth of 0.3% at the modelled terminal ROE of about 0.45% under g <= ROE x (1 - payout), and it is the policy that keeps the dividend method meaningful for an over-capitalised bank whose loan book cannot absorb its equity (CAR F13, [S12]).

flags.message: a.share_change: bear +0.0861 and bull +0 do not point opposite ways
flags.justification: The share-count shock is one-sided by construction, not a stacked bear case. The base case books no corporate action because the company has decided none (S6); the only direction the count can move on a float remedy is up, through a rights issue (PUT IV at Rp1,000, F57). The bear therefore adds 8.61% of shares with no proceeds (a discounted issue), while the bull's remedy is a controller sell-down of existing shares, which changes no share count, so its shock is zero (S6). Mirroring the bull to -8.61% would model an unsourced share cancellation or buyback, which the company has never done. The dilution is one of four bear shocks and the business scenarios carry 50% weight on the base case, so it does not by itself drive the distribution.

flags.message: expected return -57%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers. (1) A return on equity of 1.44% on a capital adequacy ratio of 87.79% [S12]: the equity base is roughly twice what the loan book can use, so the warranted P/BV on the built terminal ROE of 0.45% is about 0.01x book, so fundamental value is a small fraction of book. (2) The FY2025A provision charge of Rp154.0bn against a CKPN balance of Rp63.7bn cut net profit to Rp48.3bn, so earnings power is thin and fragile [S12]. (3) The Rp7,800 price pays about 8x book and about 290x FY2026E EPS on a 7.68% public float after two disorderly-trading suspensions [S2][S3]. What today's price implies: a reverse read is about 8x book, about 290x forward earnings and a zero dividend yield [S12], which only a change-of-control or float event can support, not the lending franchise. The konglo lens already keeps 40% of the log premium in the base regime and still lands more than half below the price.

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 605.53x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 40% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc, ff_deadline); target 3,374 vs fundamental 12-month value 14 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The lens is a regime variable, not a valuation input, and the disclosures explain it: section 4 states price over the 12-month discounted fundamental, the base regime closes 40% of the log gap on the HSC listing and the staged float deadlines, and section 6 carries the ownership table. The gap is extreme because 90.96% of the shares are held by Bank of India and affiliates (F26, [S2]) against a fundamental of a low-single-digit ROE bank; the lens keeps 60% of the log premium, not the premium itself, and the target still lands 57% below the price.
